To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a hierarchical filtering method for content based music retrieval via singing or humming.

a hierarchical filtering method can be used to filter out 80%-95% of unlikely candidates, and then compare the remaining 20%-5% candidates in a more detailed manner to retrieve the top 1-10 most similar candidates with a high success probability.

(1) the proposed hierarchical filtering method is an effective approach for content-based music information retrieval; (2) the proposed method is applicable to a wide range of multimedia information retrieval systems; and (3) the proposed method can be used to design a music search engine over the Internet or query engines in digital libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a content-based music search system that can take acoustic inputs (e.g., singing or humming) from the user, retrieve a ranked list of candidate songs from a database, and then play them back to the user.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed HFM and the analysis framework can be applied to other information retrieval systems.

the proposed HFM and the analysis framework are general and can be directly applied in a wide range of content-based information retrieval applications, including music retrieval, video retrieval, image retrieval, and text retrieval.
we have successfully developed a prototype system that can perform real-time, content-based, and accurate music search using a microphone and the Internet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a prototype of a music search engine that can take a query of a few seconds of singing or humming and return the intended song with a very high success rate.

the proposed hierarchical filtering method can be directly applied as a generic framework for other content-based multimedia retrieval applications, and Super MBox can be used as a prototype for a music search engine over the Internet.
we have developed an innovative and effective content-based music retrieval engine that can take user's acoustic input, and then retrieve a ranked list of candidate songs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a well-designed hierarchical filtering method, the performance of the content-based retrieval system can be greatly improved.
, with a little bit of training, a user can easily search for a song by singing/humming a few seconds of it, even with mediocre singing skills.
, in a real-world application of music information retrieval, a user's acoustic singing input is a much better indicator for song search than a user's text query.
